title: Cohomological description of integral adic constructible complexes
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, let $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ be a finite extension with valuation ring $R=\mathcal O_E$, uniformizer $\pi$, and residue field $k=R/(\pi)$, as in [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension], and let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], meaning that it has a finite affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. On the pro-étale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] $X_{\mathrm{proét}}$ put $B=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(R/\pi^n)_X=\mathcal O_{E,X}$, with the canonical quotient $B\to k_X$ ([det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit], [det-prop-integral-criterion-constant-coefficients]). Let $\nu_X:X_{\mathrm{proét}}\to X_{\mathrm{ét}}$ be the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. A $B$-module sheaf is constructible if it admits a finite stratification of $X$ by constructible locally closed subschemes [def-constructible-stratification] on each of which it is pro-étale locally $B\otimes_R P$ for a finitely presented $R$-module $P$ [def-sc-finitely-presented-module], [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. Use the bounded constructible cohomology condition of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible], and derived $(\pi)$-completeness in the sense of [def-weil-pbc-locally-derived-ringed-ideal-complete].

Here $\operatorname{Mod}(B)$ is the category of $B$-module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], $D$ is the unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], $X_{\mathrm{ét}}$ is the small étale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and all derived tensors are relative tensors [sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]. For every $K\in D(\operatorname{Mod}(B))$, the following are equivalent:

1. $K$ is bounded and every cohomology sheaf of $K$ is constructible as a $B$-module sheaf.
2. $K$ is derived $(\pi)$-complete and there exists a bounded complex $C\in D(X_{\mathrm{ét}},k)$ with constructible cohomology sheaves and finite Tor amplitude, together with an isomorphism $\nu_X^*C\simeq K\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}k_X$ in $D(X_{\mathrm{proét}},k_X)$.

Here finite Tor amplitude means that there are integers $a\leq b$ such that $H^i(C\otimes_{k_X}^{\mathbf L}N)=0$ for every étale $k_X$-module sheaf $N$ and every $i\notin[a,b]$. Constructible étale $k_X$-module sheaves mean those which on a finite constructible locally closed stratification are locally constant with finite-dimensional $k$-values. Torsion $R$-modules $P$ are allowed; no finite dimension of $X$ or invertibility of $\ell$ on $X$ is assumed.

source.place: Definition 6.8.10 and Proposition 6.8.11(3), with Definition 6.5.1 (completed coefficient formulation) and Definition 6.3.1 / Remark 6.3.2 (residue field constructible complexes). See also Stacks Tag 09C0, proetale.tex, section-suitable-derived, for the adic criterion.

proof.text: The ring $R$ is a DVR, hence Noetherian, by [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr]. It is $(\pi)$-adically complete: put $r=|\pi|_E\in(0,1)$. For compatible residues choose lifts $x_n\in R$; for $m\geq n$, $|x_m-x_n|_E\leq r^n$. Completeness [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-complete] gives a limit $x\in E$, and the nonarchimedean inequality [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-absolute-value] gives $|x|_E\leq1$ and $|x-x_n|_E\leq r^n$. The DVR factorization identifies the latter ball with $\pi^nR$, so $x$ realizes the given residues. An element in every $\pi^nR$ has norm at most every $r^n$, hence is zero. By [det-prop-sfb-qlbar-colimit-x-integral-limit] this completed coefficient sheaf is the given $B=\mathcal O_{E,X}$. For every scheme $S$, [det-prop-integral-criterion-constant-coefficients](1) gives flatness of $R_S\to B_S$ and $B_S/\pi B_S=k_S$. Thus the general coefficient hypotheses of [lem-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect] hold for $A=R$, $I=(\pi)$; its condition (a) is exactly condition (2) of the item.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3): coefficient specialization of Definition 6.5.1 and Proposition 6.6.11

proof.text: Every finitely presented $R$-module $P$ has a length-one finite free resolution. Indeed choose a finite surjection $R^m\twoheadrightarrow P$. Its kernel $N$ is finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], and it is torsion-free because $N\subset R^m$ and $R$ is a domain. Hence [lem-sc-dvr-fg-torsionfree-free] makes $N$ finite free. The complex $[N\to R^m]$ in degrees $-1,0$ resolves $P$. On any scheme $S$, [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-section-properties](1) makes the corresponding constant-sheaf sequence exact. Flatness from [det-prop-integral-criterion-constant-coefficients](1), interpreted using [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], keeps it exact after tensoring with $B_S$. Therefore the finite constant local model $B_S\otimes_R P$ is represented by the two-term finite free $B_S$-complex $B_S\otimes_R[N\to R^m]$. This works also for torsion $P$; it does not assume $P$ free.

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3), forward inclusion: finite projective resolution of the local module

proof.text: Let $F$ be a constructible $B$-module sheaf. By its definition in the item and [sk-def-sfb-constructible], there is a finite constructible stratification on which $F$ is pro-étale locally $B_S\otimes_R P$ with $P$ finitely presented. Step 2 supplies a perfect $R$-complex representing each such model. Apply (b)$\Rightarrow$(a) of [lem-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect] to $F[0]$. This proves that each constructible sheaf in degree zero satisfies (2).

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3), forward inclusion, reduction to a constructible sheaf; Proposition 6.6.11, reverse direction

proof.text: Assume (1), and choose $u\leq v$ with $H^q(K)=0$ outside $[u,v]$. Each $H^q(K)[-q]$ satisfies (a) by Step 3 and the shift closure in [lem-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect]. For $q=u,u+1,\ldots,v$, use the distinguished triangles of [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-triangle], $\tau_{\leq q-1}K\to\tau_{\leq q}K\to H^q(K)[-q]\to(\tau_{\leq q-1}K)[1]$. Start with $\tau_{\leq u-1}K\simeq0$ and apply the triangulated-subcategory clause of [lem-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect] at each of these finitely many triangles. This gives (a) for $\tau_{\leq v}K\simeq K$, hence (2).

source.place: Proposition 6.8.11(3), forward inclusion: finite cohomological dévissage

proof.text: Assume (2). By [lem-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect], $K$ is bounded and has a finite stratification on which it is pro-étale locally $B_S\otimes_R P^\bullet$, with $P^\bullet$ bounded finite projective. For a stratum immersion $g:S\hookrightarrow X$, inverse image preserves the constant quotient sheaves and, by [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-immersion-limit-preservation], their inverse limit. Hence $g^{-1}B\simeq\varprojlim_n(R/\pi^n)_S=B_S$, so extension along this coefficient identification is exact by the same cited statement. Restriction to an object of a pro-étale cover is induced by an exact module restriction [def-weil-pbc-ringed-derived-restriction]. These restrictions therefore commute with cohomology. Constant sheafification is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-constant-module-section-properties](1), and extension from $R_S$ to $B_S$ is exact by [det-prop-integral-criterion-constant-coefficients](1) and [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules]. Consequently the local cohomology is $B_S\otimes_R H^q(P^\bullet)$. Kernels and images of differentials in the finite modules $P^i$ are finite by [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-submodule-finite], so their cohomology quotients are finite. Each $H^q(P^\bullet)$ is finitely presented by [lem-sc-noetherian-finite-module-finite-presentation]. Thus each $H^q(K)$ has exactly the finite constant local models required for constructibility. Together with boundedness this proves (1).

Also read the blueprint sk-prop-integral-criterion text. ITEM: states 6.8.11(3) exactly. Coefficients are B=lim(R/pi^n)_X=O_{E,X}, which is BS's R-hat; torsion P is allowed; there is no dimension or ell hypothesis; the residue condition is Def 6.5.1 over the field k; completeness is the local definition, which the parent already relates to the tower notion. Nothing is weakened. STEPS: (1) the Cauchy argument proves R=lim R/pi^n; the child's (a) is literally the item's (2). (2) N in R^m is finite (00IK) and torsion-free, hence free (0AUW); exactness then follows from constant-sheaf exactness and flatness of R_S->B_S (constant-coefficients (1) and def-pc-flat). (3) The child's (b)=>(a) applies to the two-term free models. (4) The truncation-triangle induction is explicit: base 0, end tau_{<=v}K=K, u=v and K=0 covered. (5) The child gives boundedness and local perfect models; exact restrictions, constant-sheaf exactness and flatness give H^q=B_S tensor H^q(P), which is finitely presented. Each step uses only what its cited statements say. NEW NODE lem-sfb-adic-stratified-perfect: true, statement-only and self-contained; it is BS 6.5.1+6.5.3+6.6.11 specialised to a complete local A so that A/I is a field (Rem 6.3.2). Small cases tested: X empty, K=0, A a field, k[e]/e^2, a geometric point, and E_X, which is not complete. Duplicate search over the whole DAG (6.6.11/6.8.11/09C1/09C2/09C7/stratified-perfect): the near matches have extra hypotheses, are only local, or would make a cycle. It does not restate the item or the parent; the DVR resolution and the devissage stay in the item. No cycle in the 2310-node closure; the missing def-weil-pbc-etale-morphism was already missing before this delivery.
